summary: Slash is an open-source tool designed to help you save, organise, and share bookmarks and links from your own infrastructure. It provides a centralised web interface for managing collections of URLs without relying on third-party bookmarking services. As a self-hosted platform under the GPL-3.0 licence, it gives you complete control over your stored link data.
goodFor: This is a good fit if you want a dedicated, self-hosted alternative to commercial bookmark managers and prefer keeping your link collections on your own hardware.
watchOut: The repository currently shows low maintenance activity, which may mean slower responses to security issues or bug fixes. It also competes in a well-established category with many mature alternatives.
deployNotes: Since it is distributed for Docker, you will typically need to configure persistent volumes for data storage and place the container behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
